# Headless Chrome's 800 px screen clamps every script-moved popup

## Context

Several of #17844's census rows are classed environment-bound ("headed-only"). Measured today, at least one of them is bound by a single launch default: headless Chrome gives every window an **800×600 screen**, and the window manager clamps a script-moved popup into it. A test's CDP placement is not clamped, so a spec can stage a target popup off that screen, and the product's own `window.moveTo` then cannot follow it there.

## The Problem

`DemoBPerspectivesNL` stalls in its cross-window step. The conversion park moves the torn-out vessel to the target's origin with `Neo.Main.windowNativeMoveTo(822, 22)`. `#moveWindow` polls 6 × 50 ms, sees the popup at x = 320 and answers `false`, so the park is refused (`refusedAt: 'move'`) and re-proposed about every 670 ms. The tour's step never completes, and the spec's 10 s hosting poll reports "the tour has not reached its cross-window step". A main-thread trail of `parkWindowDrag` / `windowNativeMoveTo` / `windowNativeFocus` recorded the loop.

x = 320 is 800 − 480. A standalone probe with the e2e channel (`chrome`, headless) opens a 480×360 popup and calls `moveTo`:

| launch | `screen.width` | `moveTo(900, 20)` lands at | `moveTo(1400, 20)` lands at |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 800 | 320, 20 | 320, 20 |
| `--screen-info={1920x1080}` | 1920 | 900, 20 | 1400, 20 |
| `--window-size=1920,1080` | 800 | not moved | not moved |

With the overlay `--screen-info={1920x1080}`, `DemoBPerspectivesNL` passes the hosting poll: the popup hosts the live Workbench pane. It then fails at the next assertion, "worker truth must show the original instance mounted once into the popup", which is a separate question for the next owner.

## The Architectural Reality

- The e2e browser's arguments are declared once in `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs`: `BASE_LAUNCH_ARGS`, shared by `PRESENTING_LAUNCH_ARGS` and `ENGINE_LAUNCH_ARGS`. `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` launches the local `chrome` channel with `activeLaunchArgs()`.
- Specs that set `contextOptions.screen` change only what `window.screen` reports; the window manager still clamps to the real headless screen.
- `Neo.Main#moveWindow` verifies the requested coordinates, which is correct: the clamp is real, and the product reports it truthfully.

## The Fix

Give the headless browser a realistic screen: add `--screen-info={1920x1080}` to `BASE_LAUNCH_ARGS`. The switch belongs to Chrome's headless mode; this ticket must confirm that a headed run ignores it before relying on that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `BASE_LAUNCH_ARGS` carries `--screen-info={1920x1080}`, with JSDoc stating why: the clamp, plus the probe table above in short.
- [ ] AC-2: A headless census of the NL battery with the change, diffed by title against the 22 at `a9abb6c1dc` (#17844 trap 1). Each environment-bound row is re-classified: `DemoBPerspectivesNL`, `DockPlacementNL` (needs 1,620 px), `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` (needs 1,200 px) and `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` ×3. The last three are predictions, not measurements.
- [ ] AC-3: No row that is green today turns red. `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`'s rig chooses its stage by screen size (#19260) and now takes the large-stage branch; it must stay green.
- [ ] AC-4: CI's `e2e-engine` tier is green at the head, since it runs headless with these arguments.
- [ ] AC-5: A headed run shows `screen.width` equal to the real display's, proving the switch is headless-only. Run it on the operator's go, because headed runs place windows on his displays.

## Out of Scope

- `DemoBPerspectivesNL`'s next assertion (the instance mounts once into the popup): a separate ticket once measured.
- Product placement code: it reports the clamp truthfully.

**AC-3 fails: one green row turns red.** `WorkstationDragAffordancesNL › the ordinary body-mounted tab proxy has a theme-owned surface in both modes`:
- It passes without the flag and fails with it: whole file, isolated, deterministic.
- The dark pass completes, including the Escape and a proxy count of 0. The light pass's `startAuditDrag` then never sees `.neo-tab-header-toolbar.neo-is-dragging`.
- The positions are inside the scale pane, so no tear-out is involved. I have not found the cause yet.
- Users have real screens, so this may be a product defect rather than a harness one. That is why I am not narrowing the flag to hide it.

**Three more reds, not caused by the flag:**
- `DemoBDockTransactionsNL › one Group batch …` fails at `save_transaction` → `archive-store-unavailable: … Error POSTing to endpoint`. That is today's saturated Memory Core (Institution #255 / Brain #552), the same class as the transient `TransactionArchiveReplay`.
- `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL › large-over-small` ×2 are skipped on dev because the 800 px screen is too small. With the flag they run and fail (`target proxy width follows the live source viewport`). Latent large-screen reds; skipped→red, not green→red.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-26T20:28:10Z

**The AC-3 red is a start race, and the gesture never reaches the SortZone. Measured; the fix is not in yet.**

`WorkstationDragAffordancesNL › the ordinary body-mounted tab proxy …` under the flag, all runs headless with the runtime root bound:

| settle after `setWorkspaceTheme` | isolated (`test.only`) | whole file |
|---|---|---|
| none (as on `dev`) | 0/3 | 0/2 |
| two `requestAnimationFrame`s | 4/4 | 1/2, 1/3 |
| 300 ms | 3/3 | not run |

A probe dumped `app.getDragState()` and `app.getDragTrace()` when the light pass's drag did not start:
- `DragCoordinator` is idle: `pointerGestureToken: null`, `nativeGestures: []`, `activeTargetZone: null`.
- The trace's last session is the **dark** pass (`zoneId: neo-dock-tab-sortzone-4`, `startIndex: 1`), ending in `{t: 'cancel', noop: true}`.
- **No session opens for the light pass.** The second mousedown and moves never become a SortZone drag.
- The dark pass's claim trace shows `workstation-cross-window` claims on `gesture-1`, which is the cross-window machinery. My reading, still a hypothesis: that machinery engages only when the screen has room for a window, and it is why the flag moves this timing at all.

So a pointer gesture begun shortly after a cancelled drag (plus a theme switch) is not admitted, and the window is wider in a whole-file run. It could be test-only timing or a narrow product gate in the main-thread drag start; I cannot tell yet. A frame settle would make the arm green most of the time without explaining it, so I have not committed one.

Still valid from above: the flag moves `DemoBPerspectivesNL` and `DockPlacementNL` past their screen failures, and the `large-over-small` pair now has an owner (#19297, blocked by this ticket).
